title: Rocket Report: Winter is coming for Themis; Cowboy Space adds iron to the fire
gist: Weekly space-industry roundup covering a new US medium-lift entrant (Cowboy Space), Stoke Space financing, Vulcan's return to flight, ESA's Themis delays, and warnings of a launch supply crunch lasting to about 2030. SpaceX is described as prioritizing AI compute over NASA.

insights.claim: Industry executives warned that the US government may have moved too quickly in concluding the commercial launch market could support rising military demand, especially as SpaceX shifts from Falcon 9 to Starship.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Capacity shortfalls could raise launch pricing and favor providers with flight-proven vehicles.

insights.claim: A ULA executive said the supply crunch should ease as new rockets enter service, but '2030-ish is the best I would hope for right now.'
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Plan for tight launch capacity through at least 2030.
insights.quote: 2030-ish is the best I would hope for right now

insights.claim: Stoke Space's Devin Papandrew said it 'may have been a strategic error' for the government to assume the launch problem had been solved, and urged more funding and regulatory relief.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: New entrants will lobby for government support, a possible tailwind for their funding.
insights.quote: may have been a strategic error

insights.claim: Space Force leaders want a third heavy-lift spaceport operating by 2030 but have not chosen a location or how to acquire land.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Spaceport buildout is a long-lead infrastructure need with uncertain siting and public-private options.
insights.locator: Space Force says America needs a new spaceport

insights.claim: Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron, a 282-foot methane rocket with nine Clydesdale engines on the first stage and up to 18 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, targeting launch before the end of 2028.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Another entrant joins a crowded medium-lift field with little hardware shown so far.

insights.claim: Cowboy Space, founded by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt as Aetherflux in 2024, plans to turn Big Iron's upper stage into a space data center with five racks of GPUs and laser links.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Orbital AI compute is attracting capital beyond SpaceX.

insights.claim: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital made a conditional commitment of a $150 million loan to Stoke Space for a second Cape Canaveral launch pad.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Government debt financing of launch infrastructure signals national-security priority.
insights.locator: More good news for Stoke Space

insights.claim: Stoke Space raised a $1 billion Series E in September, bringing total capital raised to $2.3 billion, and aims to fly its Nova Pathfinder next year and Block 2 in 2029.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Heavy capitalization makes Stoke a credible Falcon 9 alternative.

insights.claim: ULA plans to return Vulcan to service on November 13 with 40 Amazon Leo satellites, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Vulcan's return is a key catalyst for Amazon's constellation and Space Force confidence.
insights.locator: Vulcan's return-to-flight mission has a launch date

insights.claim: Vulcan suffered solid rocket booster nozzle failures on two of its first four missions, costing it Space Force confidence even though the missions completed.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Another anomaly could threaten ULA's national security share.

insights.claim: NASA will contract ULA to develop an extended Centaur V upper stage for SLS so Orion can reach low-lunar orbit, with a return to the lunar surface as soon as 2028.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Extended Centaur replaces the costlier Exploration Upper Stage, benefiting ULA.
insights.locator: ULA to develop upgraded Centaur for SLS

insights.claim: SpaceX wants to end Crew Dragon flights by 2030 and is winding down Falcon 9 for Starship, whose capacity will be filled by Starlink and its Starmind orbital data center constellation.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: SpaceX is repositioning from government launch to AI compute, loosening its NASA ties.

insights.claim: Virgin Galactic's Delta-class rocket plane Apeiron expects its first commercial flight in early Q2 2027, and the company is the only one with a realistic chance of flying paying space passengers soon.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Dates are likely to slip, so treat 2027 timing skeptically.
insights.locator: Virgin's new rocket plane reaches home port

insights.claim: ESA's Themis reusable rocket hopper may miss its first flight in 2026 due to Scandinavian winter, after originally being expected in 2022.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: European reusability lags SpaceX by years.
insights.locator: ESA's reusable rocket testbed seems cursed
